%[** TN: \Chapter{X.}{A Chapter That Is Only a Comment}]
\Chapter{I.}{General Notions. The Principle of Conservation
of Extension-in-Phase.}

We write $q_{1}$,~\dots $q_{n}$ for the coördinates, and
\[
F_{1}\, dq_{1} + F_{2}\, dq_{2} \Add{+} \cdots + F_{n}\, dq_{n}
\Tag{(1)}
\]
for the moment of the forces, and by~\Eq{(1)}
\begin{gather*}
\eps = \efrac{1}{2} \intap \Chg{\eps}{e}^{-\eps}\, dp_{1} \dots dq_{n},
  \Tag{(2)} \displaybreak[0] \\
U = \frac{1}{2},
  \Tag{(3)}
\end{gather*}
which is what we wanted.
\PageSep{2}

\Chapter[The Function phi and the Canonical Distribution.]{II.}{The Function $\phi$ and the
Canonical Distribution.}

\Theorem{I\@.} If an ensemble of systems is so distributed in phase, then $\eps$ is least.

\Theorem{II\@.} If two ensembles are combined\Add{,} the entropy increases.
